purpose: A closed read projection for a Work Request captured from a current sourced routine answer. It specifies what an authenticated server-side reader may return; it does not add capture, triage, claim, approval, dispatch, or execution transport to the static Control Room prototype.

authority.source_reader: mcp-server search-doctrine response with current source and reconstructible provenance

transport: authenticated MCP-backed read, not implemented by this static prototype

output.human_ref: durable human-readable Work Request reference; never a database UUID

source.label_rule: exact source label from the current retrieved result; never a generated summary

triage.rule: present only for canonical triaged rows; it is durable readback, never an action authority. It stays null on a withdrawn row for a structural reason rather than a rendering choice: withdrawal is captured-only, and the canonical shape constraint requires the three triage columns to be null in both terminal states, so a withdrawn sourced request never held triage to report.

plan.rule: immutable plan hash, bounded scope summary, and persisted references only; never commands or caller-authored steps

pending_outcome_feedback.rule: null unless one latest unaccepted proposal remains bound to the exact current ready Work Request version and accepted plan; then exposes its closed safe proposal fields separately for human review after reload. It never appears in accepted history and never claims acceptance, execution, completion, success, release, or displacement.

outcome_feedback.rule: null until a human authority accepts one exact immutable evidence proposal; then exposes only the durable safe outcome readback. It is observational feedback, never execution, completion, release, approval, or a state transition.
outcome_feedback.measurement_rule: Observed minutes, interaction surface, heavy-session use, and manual context transfers are observations for later displacement comparison only. They do not claim displacement or retire an old ritual.

outcome_feedback_history.rule: the deterministic oldest-to-newest last 20 human-accepted outcome feedback receipts; pending proposals never appear
outcome_feedback_history.item: the same closed safe fields as outcome_feedback

output.accepted_feedback_count: count of all human-accepted immutable outcome feedback receipts for this Work Request; it is not a completion count

shape.rule: durable derived shape disposition and fixed surface reference only; never caller-controlled

withdrawal.rule: null unless the canonical row is declined or superseded; then it carries why the request was withdrawn, when it closed, and the request that replaced it. It exists because both terminals collapse onto one projection state, and the crosswalk's REASON SURVIVES COLLAPSE invariant obliges the projection to carry what distinguished them. It is durable readback of a closed record: it claims no completion, no success, no failure of the work, and offers no way to reopen or re-decide the request.
withdrawal.superseded_by_ref: the successor's durable human Work Request reference, never a database UUID; null on a declined row, where the canonical receipt's own check constraint forbids a successor
withdrawal.captured_only: a sourced request may be withdrawn from captured and no later state, so a withdrawal never strands a triage receipt, a shape disposition, a plan or an admission

prohibitions: derive canonical state from a UI label
render a withdrawn request as queued, or offer a human any next action on one
drop a withdrawn request from the read rather than returning its record
interpret accepted outcome feedback as success, displacement, execution, completion, or a state transition
accept a client-supplied tenant, actor, or source reference
expose a raw database UUID as the human label
copy business payload or raw question text into the projection
add POST, dispatch, claim, approve, or execute routes
integration_boundary: An authenticated server-side reader must validate tenant and actor scope, current source freshness, and provenance before returning this projection. Capture and transition ownership remain in the MCP/record-layer implementation. Outcome-feedback proposal and human acceptance remain separate record-layer writes; the reader returns the latest unaccepted proposal only in pending_outcome_feedback and accepted receipts only in outcome_feedback/history.
